prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments in Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (non-ideological)

Foundations and fiscal rules
- Adhere to fiscal rules: current budget in balance; debt falling as a share of GDP in year five; OBR oversight for fiscal events.
- No rises in National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates, or VAT.
- Tax measures: abolish non-dom status; close carried interest loophole; tighten offshore trust use for inheritance tax; modernise HMRC to counter avoidance.
- Covid Corruption Commissioner to recover pandemic-related losses; tighten public procurement standards.

Borders, security, and defence
- Strategic Defence Review in year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence.
- Maintain nuclear deterrent and NATO commitment; strengthen counter-espionage and counter-extremism; introduce Martyn’s Law.
- Create Border Security Command; hire caseworkers to clear asylum backlog; end use of hotels; establish returns/enforcement unit; seek EU security agreement.

Economy and business
- Industrial strategy with statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital for ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS, green hydrogen.
- Cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; retain full expensing and Annual Investment Allowance.
- Replace business rates in England; one major fiscal event per year; publish business tax roadmap.
- Ten-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority.
- Planning reform to speed nationally significant projects; gigabit and national 5G coverage by 2030.
- Support for AI and data (Regulatory Innovation Office; National Data Library); regulate frontier AI models.
- Small business: tackle late payments; reform British Business Bank; open procurement; strengthen Post Office and Horizon redress.

Housing and devolution
- Build 1.5 million homes over the parliament; restore mandatory housing targets; brownfield-first; strategic “grey belt” releases under rules; new towns; stronger compulsory purchase.
- Boost social and affordable housing; review Right to Buy discounts; first-refusal for first-time buyers; permanent mortgage guarantee scheme.
- Devolution bill: wider local powers (transport, skills, housing, employment support); Local Growth Plans; multi-year council settlements.

Work, immigration, and skills
- Reduce net migration; link shortages to domestic training; strengthen Migration Advisory Committee.
- New Deal for Working People: day-one rights (unfair dismissal, sick/parental leave); ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect living costs; remove adult age bands.
- Youth guarantee (18–21): training, apprenticeship, or job support; establish Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to Growth and Skills Levy.

Clean energy, climate, nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; maintain gas strategic reserve; progress Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs.
- No new oil and gas exploration licences; no fracking or new coal; extend and tighten windfall levy.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest in clean generation; Local Power Plan; grid reform; reduce standing charges.
- British Jobs Bonus (up to £500m/yr) for UK supply chains.
- Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon Border Adjustment; mandate transition plans for financial institutions/FTSE 100.
- Nature: new National River Walks; three National Forests; habitat expansion; water companies under special measures; tougher fines/bonuses rules.
- Farming: 50% public sector food local or higher-standard; reform ELM schemes; TB strategy without badger cull. Animal welfare: ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares; phase out animal testing.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders for persistent antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory YOT referral; bans on certain blades; enforce online sales rules; Young Futures hubs; youth workers in A&E/PRUs; offence of child criminal exploitation.
- Violence against women and girls: rape/SO units in every force; specialist courts; domestic abuse experts in 999; stronger stalking and spiking laws.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; inspectorate powers; safeguards on child strip-searches; expanded fraud strategy; direct entry detectives.
- Prisons: expand capacity; reduce reoffending via work, housing, treatment; strategic probation review.
- Historical cases: Hillsborough Law; act on Infected Blood, Grenfell, Covid inquiries; Windrush Commissioner; Orgreave inquiry/Investigation.

Opportunity, education, health
- Childcare: 3,000 new school-based nurseries; review parental leave; unique identifier to improve children’s services.
- Schools: 6,500 teachers (shortage subjects); leadership and inspection reform (report cards; MATs inspected); early numeracy and language; school mental health support; free breakfast clubs; limit branded uniform items; curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusion improvements.
- Arts and sport: study a creative/vocational subject to 16; National Music Education Network; ticket resale protections; football regulator.
- Equality measures: socio-economic duty; Race Equality Act; disability/ethnicity pay gap reporting; equal pay extensions; full ban on conversion practices; modernise gender recognition while retaining clinical diagnosis; uphold single-sex exceptions.
- NHS: 40,000 extra weekly appointments via extended hours; shared waiting lists; use independent capacity; workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; expand clinical trials; enhance NHS app; maternity safety targets; regulate managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership; implement Cass Review.
- Primary/community care: more GPs; face-to-face option; modern booking; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; direct referrals; trial Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- Social care: create National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement; family visiting rights; integrate with NHS.
- Mental health: 8,500 additional staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; hospital opt-out cessation; restrict child-appeal vapes; ban junk-food ads to children and high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s; online safety additions; gambling reforms; halve gap in healthy life expectancy; HIV plan to 2030.

Governance and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Adviser; Modernisation Committee; ban MPs’ paid consultancy roles.
- Immediate Lords reforms: end hereditary peers; retire at 80; participation standards; consult on replacement second chamber.
- Votes at 16; improve voter registration; strengthen donation rules; reset intergovernmental relations; Council of the Nations and Regions; devolution steps for Scotland, Wales, NI; repeal/replace NI Legacy Act per Stormont House.
- Foreign policy: strengthen alliances; improve UK–EU co-operation (veterinary deal, mutual recognition, security pact); targeted trade strategy (incl. India FTA); support Ukraine (including asset use); AUKUS; balanced China approach; Clean Power Alliance; rebuild international development capability; restore 0.7% GNI on aid when fiscally possible.
